                                         Answer: A                                       No tool used                                      Adaptive                                Tool overuse

                                        Figure 1. Motivation and effectiveness of dynamic tool invocation in CodeDance. Left: qualitative examples show that both tool underuse
                                        (unable to invoke tools on challenging tasks) and tool overuse (redundant calls on easy tasks) lead to hallucinated reasoning, incorrect
                                        answers, and unnecessary complexity (more reasoning turns and longer rollout time), whereas CodeDance dynamically invokes tools
                                        according to task difficulty to obtain correct solutions. Right: quantitative results show CodeDance-7B consistently surpasses all Qwen2.5-
                                        VL 7B baselines and exceeds the 32B version on several tasks.

                                                                                  Abstract                                                                    soning. To guide this process, we introduce a reward for
                                                                                                                                                              balanced and adaptive tool calling, which balances explo-
                                        Recent releases such as o3 highlight human-like “thinking                                                             ration with efficiency and mitigates tool overuse. Interest-
                                        with images” reasoning that combines tool use with step-                                                              ingly, beyond the expected capabilities taught by atomic su-
                                        wise verification, yet most open-source approaches still rely                                                         pervision, we empirically observe novel emergent behaviors
                                        on text-only chains, rigid visual schemas, or single-step                                                             during RL training: CodeDance demonstrates novel tool
                                        pipelines, limiting flexibility, interpretability, and transfer-                                                      invocations, unseen compositions, and cross-task transfer.
                                        ability on complex tasks. We introduce CodeDance, which                                                               These behaviors arise without task-specific fine-tuning, sug-
                                        explores executable code as a general solver for visual rea-                                                          gesting a general and scalable mechanism for executable
                                        soning. Unlike fixed-schema calls (e.g., only predicting                                                              visual reasoning. Extensive experiments across reason-
                                        bounding-box coordinates), CodeDance defines, composes,                                                               ing benchmarks (e.g., visual search, math, chart QA) show
                                        and executes code to orchestrate multiple tools, compute in-                                                          that CodeDance not only consistently outperforms schema-
                                        termediate results, and render visual artifacts (e.g., boxes,                                                         driven and text-only baselines, but also surpasses closed
                                        lines, plots) that support transparent, self-checkable rea-                                                           models such as GPT-4o and larger open-source models.

1. Introduction                                                                                           a proprietary black-box system: its internal mechanisms are
                                                                                                          inaccessible, its reasoning process is less transparent, and its
Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have made                                                        outputs cannot be systematically studied or reproduced. (3)
rapid progress, showing strong capabilities in both visual                                                Most open-source systems incorporating visual reasoning
perception and reasoning. By leveraging the language-                                                     remain restricted to predefined visual workflows, or rigid
centric chain-of-thought (CoT) mechanism [3, 40], models                                                  and schema-based pipelines (e.g., predicting bounding box
can decompose complex problems into intermediate steps,                                                   coordinates for cropping operations), which are inherently
thereby improving performance on challenging tasks. How-                                                  inflexible and task-specific, limiting transfer to new tools
ever, when extended to visual tasks, traditional CoT relies                                               and tasks [32, 33, 53, 57]. (4) Existing methods [55, 57] do
on static context, preventing models from dynamically in-                                                 not consider when a model should invoke tools, leading to
teracting with visual inputs or incorporating new observa-                                                tool underuse or overuse, as shown in Figure 1.
tions during intermediate reasoning [6, 58], creating an in-
formation bottleneck that hinders multi-round focusing and                                                   Consequently, the field still lacks an open and verifiable
validation. To address this, the o3 system [23] integrates the                                            medium that is general across tools and tasks for multi-
ability to actively seek new information through multiple                                                 modal reasoning, allowing MLLMs to dynamically com-
tool invocations, supporting iterative reasoning over visual                                              pose tools, produce intermediate artifacts, and self-check
inputs and demonstrating strong perception and analysis.                                                  their outputs in a transparent and reproducible manner. Ad-
   Research gaps. While recent models have made notable                                                   dressing this gap is crucial for achieving task-adaptive, ex-
progress, fundamental gaps remain unresolved. (1) Current                                                 plainable, and transferable reasoning across complex real-
approaches largely extend CoT into multimodal reasoning                                                   world tasks.
via text-only templates, failing to incorporate new obser-                                                   In this work, we introduce CodeDance, a multimodal
vations, refine intermediate steps, or validate its reasoning                                             reasoning framework that leverages executable code as a
against visual evidence [10, 14]. (2) In addition, o3 remains                                             unified medium for visual reasoning. Unlike prior schema-

this foundation, we employ reinforcement learning (RL) to              this end, we curate a 34K high-quality SFT dataset covering

essary steps, or underuse them, failing to leverage visual             and balanced tool use. (2) We evaluate CodeDance on more

difficulty-adaptive tool-reward mechanism that adjusts in-             ception and complex reasoning (e.g., visual search, math
centives based on task complexity, encouraging longer op-              reasoning). Across multiple benchmarks, it outperforms
eration chains for hard problems while discouraging un-                advanced closed models (e.g., GPT-4o) and larger open-
necessary calls for simple ones. This aligns learning with             source baselines (e.g., Qwen2.5-VL-32B), demonstrating
the structure of multimodal tasks, resulting in more adap-             strong perception and reasoning capabilities, and broad gen-
tive and transparent reasoning. Together, these components             eralizability. (3) Despite being trained only on atomic oper-

methods and offer an open, generalizable medium for exe-               during RL training, including spontaneous novel tool rou-
cutable visual reasoning.                                              tines, unseen operation compositions, and cross-task trans-

knowledge further shaped by RL, reflecting our design of adaptive tool invocation. These emergent patterns motivate our scaling study in
Figure 4, where we further examine whether these capabilities strengthen with larger data, longer training, and bigger models.

system [10, 11, 32, 57]. Unlike PPO [27], GRPO removes                   Background: Synthetic reasoning data for MLLM post-
the need for a separate value network by directly computing              training. High-performance MLLMs require substantial
advantages from the normalized rewards of G sampled so-                  instruction-following training data with detailed reasoning
lutions. Formally, let πθold and πθ denote the policy model              trajectories. Recent approaches include converting existing
(parameterized by θ) before and after the update, respec-                datasets using fixed templates [7, 39] or distilling knowl-
tively, both defined over the action/token space at each po-             edge from strong teacher models [4, 38, 55], with a focus
sition. For a question q sampled from a task dataset Q, a                on developing specific capabilities such as visual-centric
group of G candidate solutions τi ∼ πθold are rolled out                 reasoning [16] and mathematical problem-solving assisted
and evaluated with a reward function r(·). Building on the               by visual cues [5, 12]. However, several limitations per-
clipped surrogate objective of PPO, we write the objective               sist in existing approaches: (i) tool-grounded verification

7.2. Prompt templates

sure the reliability and consistency of synthesized data, we
design a set of standardized prompt templates tailored for                     Table 6. Prompt template for bbox generation.
different stages of the vision-language data pipeline. These
templates serve complementary purposes: (i) In Table 5:                Please detect the entire object that most matches the ques-
assessing the informativeness of candidate images to guar-             tion in the image.
antee sufficient visual complexity for fine-grained reason-            Question: {question}
ing; (ii) In Table 6: labeling and locating the objects that
                                                                       If the target is part of an object, you need to give the bbox
most match the question. (iii) In Table 7: validating the
                                                                       of the entire object.
quality of automatically generated visual question–answer
pairs; (iv) In Table 8: enforcing a structured step-by-step
reasoning process with explicit final answers; and (v) In Ta-          For each object, return:
ble 9: enhancing reasoning accuracy by incorporating code              - ’label’: the object name
interpreter support for precise numerical or logical calcu-            - ’bbox_2d’: the object’s bounding box coordinates as
lations. Together, these prompt templates provide a com-               [x1, y1, x2, y2].
prehensive and systematic framework for controlling data
quality during synthesis, thereby improving the robustness
and utility of the resulting multimodal datasets.                      Respond in a JSON array, where each entry is a dictio-

Figure 7. Overview of the SFT dataset curation pipeline. Top: Weak-to-strong filtering. Candidate samples from diverse domains
(mathematics, science, visual reasoning, charts) are validated for quality and correctness through automated inspector modules. A weak
VLM removes trivial or low-information cases, while a stronger VLM further stratifies the remaining data into medium- and hard-difficulty
sets. Middle: Multi-turn atomic supervision. The curated data are organized into three categories. (a) Predefined image operations (e.g.,
crop, resize, rotate), where medium samples produce single-turn trajectories and hard samples produce multi-turn reasoning with interpreter
feedback. (b) Mathematical reasoning, where language-based CoT traces are decomposed into step-level atomic operations and converted
into executable code. (c) Open-ended visual operations (e.g., drawing, annotation), where questions, feedback, and snippet verification
form multi-turn executable trajectories. Bottom: Example executable snippets illustrating the supervision format across image processing,
symbolic computation, and visual annotation. A detailed curation pipeline example is shown in Figure 8.

                                                                       15
                                 Table 9. Prompt template for revised thinking with code interpreter.

   You are a helpful AI assistant. Initially, when solving a question, you would need to think step by step, without the
   ability to use code for calculation. Now, you have the capability to write code to use the code interpreter for calculation.
   The code will be executed by a sandbox, and the result can be returned to enhance your reasoning process. You can
   now leverage code to enhance your calculation while still maintaining the reasoning process.
   The thinking process can have multiple code snippets. Each code snippet is wrapped with
   <code>
   ‘‘‘python
   code snippet
   ‘‘‘
   </code>

   The returned result is wrapped with
   <interpreter> execution results</interpreter>

   Goal: Modify the original thinking process to make it more accurate by replacing manual calculation steps that can
   benefit from code execution with the corresponding code snippets and their interpreter’s execution results. The core
   reasoning logic from the original thinking process, including any unsuccessful attempts, should remain unchanged.
   You should only replace the necessary manual calculation steps with code and interpreter’s execution results, without
   altering the rest tokens of the thinking process.
   User Question: {question}
   Original Thinking Process (without code interpreter’s support):
   <original_thinking_process> {original_response} </original_thinking_process>

   Details:
   1. Identify sections where code execution could speed up the reasoning process or make the calculation more accurate.
   For simple calculations, you should keep the original text-based reasoning process without executing any code.
   2. Replace the manual calculation steps with code snippets and the corresponding interpreter’s execution results.
   3. Keep the logical flow of the reasoning process intact, including any failed exploration attempts that were part of the
   initial process.
   4. The code snippets should be complete scripts, including necessary imports.
   5. Outputs in the code snippets must explicitly call the print function.
   6. Execution results should match the model’s output exactly, with no extra or missing tokens.
   7. If, during the revised thinking process, you obtain the same result as in the original reasoning, you may omit
   numerical computations and refrain from simplifying to specific numeric values.
   8. If the Original Thinking Process does not include an <answer> section at the end, please add it:
   <answer> \boxed{{’The final answer goes here.’}} </answer>

   Revised Thinking Process (With code interpreter’s support):

magnitude and shape of the dips.                                       vocation and program logic (e.g., sequencing, conditionals,

get, whereas agent systems often require additional policies                              tomation, and generated visual artifacts might be misused to

    In addition, given realistic compute constraints, most of                             ommend pairing such systems with appropriate safeguards,
our experiments in this work are conducted with 7B-scale                                  including safety filters, usage constraints, and responsible
models (e.g., Qwen-2.5-VL-7B), where we already observe                                   deployment practices. By doing so, the benefits of exe-
promising effects: consistent gains across general under-                                 cutable visual reasoning can be realized while minimizing
standing and complex reasoning benchmarks, and the emer-                                  the potential for misuse.
gence of new behaviors (e.g., novel tool use and tool com-
positions of atomic skills to new tasks). These empirical ob-                             12. Limitations and future work
servations are easier to scale within a single dense model,
                                                                                          Limitations. While our method demonstrates promising
while agent pipelines introduce many interacting modules
                                                                                          emergent behaviors and strong performance across diverse
that complicate both training and deployment. Overall, our
                                                                                          visual reasoning tasks, several limitations remain. First,
design favors simplicity, efficiency, and scalability, making
                                                                                          the reliance on high-quality synthetic trajectories implies
it a more practical foundation for future progress.
                                                                                          that certain real-world reasoning patterns may be under-
                                                                                          represented, potentially limiting robustness in open-domain
11. Broader impact                                                                        scenarios. Second, although code provides a general inter-
This work contributes toward building more transparent and                                face, extending to richer modalities (e.g., audio) or domain-
verifiable multimodal reasoning systems by adopting exe-                                  specific tools (e.g., medical applications) will require ad-
cutable code as the unified medium for tool use. The abil-                                ditional engineering. Finally, due to compute constraints,
ity to generate interpretable traces and intermediate artifacts                           our evaluations are primarily conducted on 7B-scale mod-
can benefit applications where accountability and auditabil-                              els; the scalability of emergent behaviors at larger scales
ity are essential, such as scientific analysis and education.                             remains to be systematically examined. Nevertheless, our
At the same time, code-generating models pose risks: ma-                                  preliminary experiments suggest a promising trend when
licious users could potentially exploit them for unsafe au-                               scaling up model capacity and compute resources.

                                                                                                           21
Future Work. Our framework demonstrates the potential
of multimodal reasoning models to support natural conver-
sations with seamless and proactive tool use through ex-
ecutable code, thereby enabling more advanced problem-
solving capabilities. Looking ahead, we envision that the
ability to “think with images” will evolve beyond the vision
modality and fixed schemas, fostering novel tool discovery
and the spontaneous composition of tools in a more gener-
alized and efficient manner. Such directions may ultimately
pave the way toward multimodal agents that are both versa-
tile and adaptive across diverse domains.
